title: January
summary: A new year, an old name, and a trail across the Channel.
question: How did January get its name?
completion: January’s older English forms came through French from Latin Ianuarius. Italian gennaio is another branch of that family.
partner: A similar sound is a clue. Let’s check the evidence.

nodes.meaning: Janus’s month. Janus was the Roman god of doors and beginnings.

evidence.title: A Roman calendar clue
evidence.text: Ianuarius named the month for Janus, the Roman god of doors, gateways and beginnings. He was pictured with two faces looking in opposite directions. Imagine January as a doorway into a new year. This Latin name lies behind the English and French forms.
